title: IAEA mission led by Rafael Grossi reaches the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant
body:
On 1 September 2022, a team of the International Atomic Energy Agency led by Director General Rafael Mariano Grossi reached the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant in southern Ukraine. The group, formally called the IAEA Support and Assistance Mission to Zaporizhzhya, had 14 members drawn from nuclear safety, security and safeguards staff. Before leaving Kyiv, Grossi said the team was moving while accepting that the risks were very high.

Russian forces had seized the plant in March 2022. On 25 August, fires caused by shelling cut the last power line connecting the plant to Ukraine's grid, forcing reactors 5 and 6 to shut down and diesel generators to start. On the morning of 1 September, shelling struck a 330-kilovolt backup line and reactor 5 was shut down.

The inspectors toured the facility and spoke with staff of Energoatom, Ukraine's state nuclear company. After the visit Grossi said it was obvious that the physical integrity of the plant had been violated several times. The IAEA said it would establish a permanent presence at the site and a few experts remained there when most of the delegation left. The agency has no authority to order a ceasefire or create a demilitarised zone around the plant.
